what_it_does: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is a technique that lets a server perform computations on encrypted data without ever decrypting it — useful for privacy-preserving cloud computing — but it is notoriously slow, requiring thousands of times more computation than working on unencrypted numbers. The core bottleneck is an operation called the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), which is a specialized version of the well-known Fast Fourier Transform adapted to work on encrypted integers; it is memory-intensive and stalls constantly waiting for data to arrive from memory. WarpDrive accelerates FHE on a standard GPU by three coordinated changes: restructuring the NTT arithmetic to cut the number of instructions by 73%, carefully interleaving memory loads to fill the wait times and eliminate 86% of pipeline stalls, and running the GPU's two types of math units — the general-purpose CUDA cores and the matrix-multiplication tensor cores (the GPU's dedicated array of fast multipliers, normally reserved for AI workloads) — simultaneously within a single NTT computation, making fuller use of the chip's total hardware.
